*Translator's note:* *Heb* “was old, coming into the days” (i.e., advancing in years).

*Translator's note:* Or “garments.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “said to.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “let them seek for my master, the king, a young girl, a virgin.” The third person plural subject of the verb is indefinite (see GKC 460 §144.*f*). The appositional expression, “a young girl, a virgin,” is idiomatic; the second term specifically defines the more general first term (see *IBHS* 230 §12.3b).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and she will stand before the king.” The Hebrew phrase “stand before” can mean “to attend; to serve” (BDB 764 s.v. עָמַד).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and she will lie down in your bosom.” The expression might imply sexual intimacy (see {{2 Samuel 12:3|2 Sam 12:3}} [where the lamb symbolizes Bathsheba] and {{Micah 7:5|Mic 7:5}}), though v. {{2 Samuel 23:4|4b}} indicates that David did not actually have sex with the young woman.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and my master, the king, will be warm.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “through all the territory of Israel.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “did not know her.” The verb יָדַע (yadaʿ, “to know”) is a euphemism for sexual relations.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “son of Haggith,” but since this formula usually designates the father (who in this case was David), the translation specifies that David was Adonijah’s father.

*Study note:* *Haggith* was one of David’s wives ({{2 Samuel 3:4|2 Sam 3:4}}; 2 Chr 3:2).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “lifting himself up.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “saying.”

*Translator's note:* Or “he acquired for himself.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to run ahead of him.”

*Translator's note:* Or “disciplined.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “did not correct him from his days.” The phrase “from his days” means “from his earliest days,” or “ever in his life.” See GKC 382 §119.*w*, n. 2.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and she gave birth to him after Absalom.” This does not imply they had the same mother; Absalom’s mother was Maacah, not Haggith ({{2 Samuel 3:4|2 Sam 3:4}}).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “his words were.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “helped after” (i.e., stood by).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Adonijah.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“him”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
*Text-critical note:* The ancient Greek version omits this appositional phrase.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Have you not heard?”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and our master David does not know.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “now, come.” The imperative of הָלַךְ (halakh) is here used as an introductory interjection. See BDB 234 s.v. חָלַךְ.

*Translator's note:* Or “so that.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “come, go to.” The imperative of הָלַךְ (halakh) is here used as an introductory interjection. See BDB 234 s.v. חָלַךְ.

*Translator's note:* Or “swear an oath to.”

*Translator's note:* In the Hebrew text the sentence is introduced by the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”), which here draws attention to Nathan’s concluding word of assurance and support. For this use of the word, see *HALOT* 252 s.v. הִנֵּה.

*Text-critical note:* The Hebrew text reads, “I will come after you.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “fill up [i.e., confirm] your words.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “bowed low and bowed down to.”

*Text-critical note:* Instead of עַתָּה (ʿattah, “now”) many Hebrew mss, along with the Old Greek, Syriac Peshitta, and Latin Vulgate, have the similar sounding independent pronoun אַתָּה (ʾattah, “you”). This reading is followed in the present translation.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “you do not know [about it].”

*Text-critical note:* Many Hebrew mss have עַתָּה (ʿattah, “now”) rather than the similar sounding independent pronoun אַתָּה (ʾattah, “you”).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the eyes of all Israel are upon you to declare to them who will sit on the throne of my master the king after him.”

*Translator's note:* The words “if a decision is not made” are added for clarification.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “lies down with his fathers.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “I and my son Solomon.” The order has been reversed in the translation for stylistic reasons.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “will be guilty”; NASB “considered offenders”; TEV “treated as traitors.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “look.” The particle הִנֵּה (hinneh) here draws attention to Nathan’s arrival and invites the audience to view the scene through the eyes of the participants.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “ground.” Since this was indoors, “floor” is more appropriate than “ground.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “look.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “eating and drinking.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “let the king, Adonijah, live!”

*Text-critical note:* Many Hebrew mss and ancient textual witnesses agree with the *Qere* in reading this as singular, “your servant.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “From my master the king is this thing done, and you did not make known to your servants who will sit on the throne of my master the king after him?”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “answered and said.”

*Study note:* *Summon Bathsheba*. Bathsheba must have left the room when Nathan arrived (see {{1 Kings 1:22|1:22}}).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “she came before the king and stood before the king.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “bowed low, face [to] the ground, and bowed down to the king.”
*Study note:* *Summon*…*Nathan*. Nathan must have left the room when Bathsheba reentered.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the king.”

*Translator's note:* The plural form is used in the Hebrew text to indicate honor and authority.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “mount Solomon my son on the mule that belongs to me and take him down to Gihon.”
*Translator's note:* Or “designate” (i.e., by anointing with oil).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “answered and said.”

*Translator's note:* Or “Amen.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “So may the Lord God of my master the king say.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my master King David.”

*Study note:* The *Kerethites* and *Pelethites* were members of David’s royal guard (see {{2 Samuel 8:18|2 Sam 8:18}}). The Kerethites may have been descendants of an ethnic group originating in Crete.

*Study note:* *A horn filled with oil*. An animal’s horn was used as an oil flask in the anointing ceremony.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the horn of oil.” This has been specified as olive oil in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* Or “anointed.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and all the people went up after him, and the people were playing flutes and rejoicing with great joy and the ground split open at the sound of them.” The verb בָּקַע (baqaʿ, “to split open”), which elsewhere describes the effects of an earthquake, is obviously here an exaggeration for the sake of emphasis.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “And Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard, now they had finished eating.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Why is the city’s sound noisy?”

*Translator's note:* The Hebrew text has “look” at this point. The particle הִנֵּה (hinneh), “look” draws attention to Jonathan’s arrival and invites the audience to view the scene through the eyes of the participants.

*Translator's note:* Or “surely.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “you are a man of strength [or “ability”] and you bring a message [that is] good.” Another option is to understand the phrase אִישׁ חַיִל (ʾish khayil) in the sense of “a worthy man,” that is “loyal.” See also {{1 Kings 1:52|1 Kgs 1:52}} and *HALOT* 311 s.v. חַיִל.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “answered and said.”

*Translator's note:* For a similar use of אֲבָל (ʾaval), see {{Genesis 17:19|Gen 17:19}}, where God rejects Abraham’s proposal and offers an alternative.

*Translator's note:* The plural form is used in the Hebrew text to indicate honor and authority.
*Translator's note:* I.e., designated by anointing with oil.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “And also Solomon sits on the throne of the kingdom.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to bless.”

*Translator's note:* The plural form is used in the Hebrew text to indicate honor and authority.

*Text-critical note:* Many Hebrew mss agree with the *Qere* in reading simply “God.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “make the name of Solomon better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne.” The term שֵׁם (shem, “name”) is used here of one’s fame and reputation.

*Translator's note:* Or “bowed down; worshiped.”

*Translator's note:* The Hebrew text reads, “and the king said.”

*Translator's note:* Or “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who….” In this blessing formula אֲשֶׁר (ʾasher, “who; because”) introduces the reason why the one being blessed deserves the honor.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and my eyes are seeing.”

*Study note:* *Grabbed hold of the horns of the altar*. The “horns” of the altar were the horn-shaped projections on the four corners of the altar (see {{Exodus 27:2|Exod 27:2}}). By going to the holy place and grabbing hold of the horns of the altar, Adonijah was seeking asylum from Solomon.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “King Solomon.” The name and title have been replaced by the pronoun (“you”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

*Translator's note:* Or “swear an oath to.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “if he is a man of strength [or ability].” In this context, where Adonijah calls himself a “servant,” implying allegiance to the new king, the phrase אִישׁ חַיִל (ʾish khayil) probably carries the sense of “a worthy man,” that is, “loyal” (see *HALOT* 311 s.v. חַיִל).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “but if evil is found in him.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “sent and they brought him down.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Go to your house.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the days of David approached to die.”

*Translator's note:* Or “commanded.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “going the way of all the earth.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “keep the charge of the Lord your God.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “by walking in his ways.”

*Translator's note:* Or “keeping.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “then you will cause to succeed all which you do and all which you turn there.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “then the Lord will establish his word which he spoke to me, saying.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “guard their way.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “by walking before me in faithfulness.”

*Translator's note:* Or “soul.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “saying.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “there will not be cut off from you a man from upon the throne of Israel.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “what he did to the two commanders…and he killed them.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he shed the blood of battle in peace.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he shed the blood of battle on his belt which is on his waist and on his sandal[s] which are on his feet.” That is, he covered himself with guilt and his guilt was obvious to all who saw him.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “according to your wisdom.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and do not bring down his grey hair in peace [to] Sheol.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “do loyalty with”; or “act faithfully toward.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and let them be among the ones who eat [at] your table.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “thus drew near to.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Look, with you is Shimei….”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he cursed me with a horrible curse on the day I went to Mahanaim.”

*Translator's note:* Or “swore an oath to.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “kill you.”

*Text-critical note:* The Lucianic recension of the Old Greek and the Vulgate have here “you” rather than “now.” The two words are homonyms in Hebrew.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “what you should do to him.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “bring his grey hair down in blood [to] Sheol.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and David lay down with his fathers.”

*Study note:* The phrase *the City of David* refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See {{2 Samuel 5:7|2 Sam 5:7}}.

*Translator's note:* Or “kingship.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “set their face to me to be king.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the kingdom turned about and became my brother’s, for from the Lord it became his.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Do not turn back my face.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “She said, ‘Speak!’”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Say to Solomon the king, for he will not turn back your face, that he might give to me Abishag the Shunammite for a wife.”

*Translator's note:* Or “meet.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “he set up a throne for the mother of the king.”

*Translator's note:* Or “I’d like to make just one request of you.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Do not turn back my face.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and the king said to her.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “So may God do to me, and so may he add.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “if with his life Adonijah has not spoken this word.”

*Translator's note:* The Hebrew text adds, “by the hand of.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and he struck him and he died.”

*Translator's note:* Or “field.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “you are a man of death,” an idiom.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and because you suffered through all which my father suffered.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “turned after” (also later in this verse).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Joab.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

*Study note:* *Grabbed hold of the horns of the altar*. The “horns” of the altar were the horn-shaped projections on the four corners of the altar (see {{Exodus 27:2|Exod 27:2}}). By going to the holy place and grabbing hold of the horns of the altar, Joab was seeking asylum from Solomon.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and it was related to King Solomon.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “so Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “saying, “In this way Joab spoke and in this way he answered me.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “house.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “take away the undeserved bloodshed which Joab spilled from upon me and from upon the house of my father.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “The Lord will cause his blood to return upon his head.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “because he struck down two men more innocent and better than he and he killed them with the sword, and my father David did not know.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “struck him and killed him.” The referent (Joab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “over.”

*Text-critical note:* The Old Greek translation includes after v. {{1 Kings 2:35|35}} some fourteen verses that are absent from the MT.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “sent and summoned.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and you may not go out from there here or there.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “your blood will be upon your head.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Good is the word, as my master the king has spoken.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “so your servant will do.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “many days.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “sent and summoned.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Is it not [true]…?” In the Hebrew text the statement is interrogative; the rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course it is.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “here or there.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “good is the word; I have heard.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Why have you not kept the oath [to] the Lord and the commandment I commanded you?”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “You know all the evil, for your heart knows, which you did to David my father.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “The Lord will cause your evil to return upon your head.”

*Translator's note:* “The king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada and he went out and struck him down and he died.”

*Translator's note:* “And the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon.”
*Study note:* The phrase *City of David* refers here to the fortress of Zion in Jerusalem, not to Bethlehem. See {{2 Samuel 5:7|2 Sam 5:7}}.

*Study note:* *Offering sacrifices at the high places*. The “high places” were places of worship that were naturally or artificially elevated.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “for the name of the Lord.” The word “name” sometimes refers to one’s reputation or honor (thus the translation here, “to honor the Lord”). The “name” of the Lord sometimes designates the Lord himself, being indistinguishable from the proper name.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “by walking in.”

*Translator's note:* Or “policies, rules.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “for it was the great high place.”

*Translator's note:* Or, “customarily offered up.” The verb form is an imperfect, which is probably used here in a customary sense to indicate continued or repeated action in past time. See GKC 314 §107.*b*.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “did.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “walked before.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “in faithfulness and in innocence and in uprightness of heart with you.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and you have kept to him this great loyalty and you gave to him a son [who] sits on his throne as this day.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and I do not know going out or coming in.”

*Translator's note:* There is no verb expressed in the Hebrew text; “stands” is supplied in the translation for clarification.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “your people whom you have chosen.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “a hearing heart.” (The Hebrew term translated “heart” often refers to the mental faculties.)

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to judge.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to understand between good and evil.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “for”; the word “otherwise” is used to reflect the logical sense of the statement.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “who is able?” The rhetorical question anticipates the answer, “no one.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “to judge.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “your numerous people.”

*Translator's note:* The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here and in v.{{1 Kings 3:15|15}} is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “And the thing was good in the eyes of the Lord, for Solomon asked for this thing.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “because you asked for this thing, and did not ask for yourself many days and did not ask for yourself riches and did not ask for the life of your enemies, but you asked for yourself understanding to hear judgment.”

*Translator's note:* This statement is introduced in the Hebrew text by the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”) which draws attention to and emphasizes what follows.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “I am doing according to your words.” The perfect tense is sometimes used of actions occurring at the same time a statement is made.

*Translator's note:* This statement is introduced by the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”) which draws attention to and emphasizes what follows. The translation assumes that the perfect tense here indicates that the action occurs as the statement is made (i.e., “right now I give you”).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “heart.” (The Hebrew term translated “heart” often refers to the mental faculties.)

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “so that there has not been one like you prior to you, and after you one will not arise like you.”

*Translator's note:* The translation assumes that the perfect tense here indicates that the action occurs as the statement is made.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “so that there is not one among the kings like you all your days.” The LXX lacks the words “all your days.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “walk in my ways.”

*Translator's note:* Or “keeping.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “walked.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “I will lengthen your days.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and look, a dream.”

*Translator's note:* Or “tokens of peace”; NIV, TEV “fellowship offerings.”
*Study note:* *There was no one else in the house except the two of us*. In other words, there were no other witnesses to the births who could identify which child belonged to which mother.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “look.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “look, it was not my son to whom I had given birth.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “they spoke before the king.” Another option is to translate, “they argued before the king.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the woman whose son was alive.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “for her compassions grew warm for her son.”

*Translator's note:* The infinitive absolute before the negated jussive emphasizes the main verb.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “feared,” perhaps in the sense, “stood in awe of.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “saw.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the wisdom of God was in his midst for performing justice.” The phrase “wisdom of God” may be taken as an attributive genitive, “divine wisdom,” or as a genitive of source, “wisdom from God.” Even in English they are basically the same, since wisdom from God is divine in character.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “were scribes”; NASB, NIV, NRSV “secretaries”; TEV, NLT “court secretaries.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “was over.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “close associate of”; KJV, ASV, NASB “the king’s friend” (a title for an adviser, not just an acquaintance).

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “over the house.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “was over.”

*Study note:* *The work crews*. This Hebrew word (מַס, mas) refers to a group of laborers conscripted for royal or public service.

Beginning with 6:1 the numbering of verses in the English Bible and the Hebrew text is again the same.

*Study note:* *From the middle of the iron-smelting furnace*. The metaphor of a furnace suggests fire and heat and is an apt image to remind the people of the suffering they endured while slaves in Egypt.

*Translator's note:* The Hebrew term כּוּר (kur, “furnace,” cf. Akkadian kūru) is a metaphor for the intense heat of purification. A כּוּר was not a source of heat but a crucible (“iron-smelting furnace”) in which precious metals were melted down and their impurities burned away (see I. Cornelius, *NIDOTTE* 2:618-19). Thus Egypt served not as a place of punishment for the Israelites, but as a place of refinement to bring Israel to a place of submission to divine sovereignty.
